claims.claim: Laravel for the core (accounts, dashboards, config, message storage, billing, webhooks, API) ... none of it is hard to scale at 50,000 widgets
claims.measured: php-laravel 681 req/s plaintext, 149 req/s single DB query per CPU
claims.why: The measurements give per-core throughput but not the request rate the core app would see at 50,000 widgets, so there is nothing to compare against.

claims.claim: Laravel Reverb as the realtime layer, running as its own long-lived process on one or two VMs (implying it can hold the widget connections)
claims.why: Reverb was not benchmarked, and no test measures WebSocket connection capacity.

claims.claim: Elixir/Phoenix is the strongest fit for this workload; it was built for huge numbers of idle connections
claims.measured: I/O-wait test with 256 connections: 18,711 req/s, p99 19.16 ms, 160 MB
claims.why: The largest test used 256 short-request connections, not tens of thousands of idle long-lived ones, so the claim about idle connections can't be checked.

claims.claim: Node with Socket.IO or Go: both can handle this (tens of thousands of live connections)
claims.why: Socket.IO wasn't tested and no benchmark measures holding thousands of persistent connections.

claims.claim: Laravel Octane is built for fast request handling
claims.measured: Octane 1,172 vs Laravel 681 req/s plaintext; 1,224 vs 705 JSON; 732 vs 149 single DB query
claims.why: Octane measured about 1.7x to 5x faster than plain Laravel on the request-handling tests, though it is still slower than almost every non-PHP server.

claims.claim: Octane is not suited to holding tens of thousands of open sockets
claims.measured: I/O-wait test with 256 connections: 86 req/s, p50 1,993 ms, p99 3,001 ms, 17% CPU
claims.why: Octane already fell apart with only 256 concurrent waiting connections, worse than plain Laravel's 591 req/s, which supports the claim even though tens of thousands weren't tested.

claims.claim: Plain PHP-FPM with polling wastes money and feels slow
claims.why: Polling wasn't benchmarked, so its cost and perceived latency compared with push can't be checked.

claims.claim: PHP-FPM and queue workers can't hold sockets
claims.measured: I/O-wait test with 256 connections: 591 req/s, p50 413 ms
claims.why: This is a claim about how PHP-FPM is built, and no test measured holding persistent sockets.

claims.claim: 50,000 idle WebSocket connections is achievable on a few well-tuned boxes
claims.why: No benchmark measures WebSocket connection counts or memory per connection.
